R45-PROD-U-061.reading: the Python reference holds the setpoint at every tolerance level (P_dev below 1e-4) while the Rust integrator, whose growing-mode guard prevents an accepted step from damping a growing mode, shows the excursion at every level (P_dev 0.018 .. 0.024); tightening the Python tolerance by five orders of magnitude does not resolve the mode, so the tightened Python answer is not a converged answer on this loop

evidence.R45-PROD-U-045 (related, seeding-sensiti: max Re lambda 1.1e-2 at 9 of 24 phases, phase 0 stable: Python N 0.048, T1 1.0e-4, T2 7.6e-6; Rust N / T1 / T2 7.6e-6: whether the excursion appears depends on how the growing phases are seeded

mechanism: as DIV-P-REF-01: a growing mode started below the tolerance scale is not seen by the error control, which integrates the unstable loop as a held setpoint and returns ok; the T1 / T2 runs inherit the effect. A loop that starts at an unstable equilibrium stays there in exact arithmetic, and its growth is seeded only by rounding and truncation noise, so no tolerance level makes the time-domain answer well posed (coordinator decision 2026-10-07, contract v8)
consequence: DIV-P-REF-01 extends from the nominal run to the tightened runs: on closed loops that are unstable at an equilibrium of their event sequence (or at a quasi-static orbit phase), no Python transient output (P42 transient_run, P43 transient_case, P45 orbit_simulated, at any registered rtol) is a trustworthy comparison target

contract v8 therefore scores the unstable stratum only on well-posed quantities (the input-only stability class and the leading eigenvalues) and reports its time-domain outputs labelled ILL_POSED_UNSTABLE_EQUILIBRIUM; the Rust transient carries the typed status UNSTABLE_EQUILIBRIUM (DIV-P-04)
the reference itself is not changed; no Python result, golden or fixture is rewritten
